title: Equal Pairwise LCMs in Dense Sets
content:
Erdős Problem #536: If $A \subseteq \{1, \ldots, N\}$ has density $|A| \geq \varepsilon N$, must there exist distinct $a, b, c \in A$ with $[a,b] = [b,c] = [a,c]$?

The condition fails for four elements (Erdős). Weisenberg showed it holds when $\varepsilon > 221/225$ and constructed sets avoiding the property with $|A| \gg (\log\log N)^{f(N)} \cdot N/\log N$. The problem remains open for general $\varepsilon > 0$.

This connects **multiplicative number theory** (LCM structure) to **density Ramsey theory** (forcing structure in dense sets).
mathContext: $A \subseteq [N]$, $|A| \geq \varepsilon N$ $\stackrel{?}{\Rightarrow}$ $\exists a \neq b \neq c \in A$: $[a,b] = [b,c] = [a,c]$. Known for $\varepsilon > 221/225$.

title: Equal Pairwise LCM Triple
content:
**HasEqualPairwiseLCM a b c**: Three distinct natural numbers have equal pairwise LCMs: $a 
eq b \wedge b 
eq c \wedge a 
eq c$ and $[a,b] = [b,c] = [a,c]$. The LCM is computed via `Nat.lcm`. This forces a rigid multiplicative structure: if the common LCM is $L$, then $a, b, c$ all divide $L$, and each pair must jointly cover every prime power in the factorization of $L$.

title: LCM Triple in a Set
content: **HasLCMTriple A**: The set $A$ contains three elements forming an equal pairwise LCM triple. Formally, $\exists a\, b\, c \in A, \text{HasEqualPairwiseLCM}(a, b, c)$. This is the property that the density conjecture asserts must hold for large dense subsets of $\{1,\ldots,N\}$.

title: Erdős Problem #536: Density Conjecture
content: **erdos_536_conjecture**: Axiomatizes the main conjecture: for every $\varepsilon > 0$, there exists $N_0$ such that for all $N \geq N_0$, any $A \subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\}$ with $|A| \geq \varepsilon N$ contains an LCM triple. This is a density Ramsey-type statement—positive density forces multiplicative structure. The conjecture is analogous to Szemerédi's theorem but for a multiplicative rather than additive pattern.

title: Weisenberg's Partial Result: ε > 221/225
content: **weisenberg_dense_case**: Axiomatizes that the conjecture holds for the specific density threshold $\varepsilon > 221/225 \approx 0.982$. This means sets containing more than 98.2% of $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ must contain an LCM triple. The bound $221/225 = 1 - 4/225$ is remarkably close to 1, leaving only a narrow gap to the full conjecture. The proof uses the fact that very dense sets must contain many divisor pairs.

title: Four-Element Analogue Fails
content: **four_elements_fail**: Axiomatizes that the quadruple analogue is false: for every $N$, there exists $A \subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\}$ with $|A| \geq N/2$ such that no four distinct elements have all $\binom{4}{2} = 6$ pairwise LCMs equal. The Lean formalization explicitly lists all six pairwise LCM equalities. This sharp contrast between triples and quadruples shows the problem sits at a critical boundary.
mathContext: $\forall N,\; \exists A \subseteq [N] : |A| \geq N/2 \wedge \nexists\, a,b,c,d \in A\text{ with all pairwise LCMs equal}$

title: Weisenberg's Construction: Large Triple-Free Sets
content: **weisenberg_construction**: Axiomatizes that there exists an unbounded function $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ (i.e., $\forall k, \exists N_0, \forall N \geq N_0, f(N) > k$) such that for every $N > 1$, there is a triple-free $A \subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\}$ with $|A| \geq f(N)$. This shows triple-free sets can be arbitrarily large, though their density tends to 0. The actual size is $\gg (\log\log N)^{g(N)} \cdot N / \log N$.

title: LCM Divisibility Structure Lemma
content: **lcm_structure**: Axiomatizes that if $\text{HasEqualPairwiseLCM}(a, b, c)$ and $[a,b] = L$, then $a \mid L$, $b \mid L$, and $c \mid L$. This follows from the definition of LCM: $[a,b] = L$ implies $a \mid L$ and $b \mid L$, and $[a,c] = L$ implies $c \mid L$. The lemma shows that an LCM triple must consist of three divisors of a common value.
mathContext: $[a,b] = [b,c] = [a,c] = L \Rightarrow a \mid L \wedge b \mid L \wedge c \mid L$
